theme: The steps of a man are established by the LORD
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 37:23-40 slowly, twice. This is the second half of the great wisdom psalm. The themes continue: the patient confidence of the righteous, the certain end of the wicked. As you read, listen for the personal note David sounds, his own life experience speaking.
settingTheScene: The second half of Psalm 37 continues the meditation on the long view. The psalmist now adds his personal testimony: “I have been young, and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken.” David has lived through enough to know how God’s economy works. The patient eventually receive. The wicked eventually fall. The promise of the meek inheriting the land continues to anchor the psalm.
observation: Verse 23: “The steps of a man are established by the LORD, when he delights in his way.” God orders the path of his people.
Verse 24: “Though he fall, he shall not be cast headlong, for the LORD upholds his hand.” Falls happen, but recovery follows.
Verse 25 is David’s personal testimony: “I have been young, and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken.”
Verses 27-29: Turn from evil, do good, dwell forever. The righteous have the long inheritance.
Verses 30-31 describe the speech and heart of the righteous: “the law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not slip.”
Verse 34: “Wait for the LORD and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land.”
Verses 35-36: The wicked man flourished like a green tree, but when the psalmist looked again, he was gone.
Verses 37-38: “Mark the blameless… for there is a future for the man of peace.”
The psalm closes: “The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD; he is their stronghold in the time of trouble.”
interpretation:
The second half of Psalm 37 deepens what the first half established. Trust the LORD. Wait for him. The wicked will pass; the righteous will inherit. But now David adds personal witness. He has lived a long life. He has seen things. And what he has seen confirms what the psalm has been saying.

Verse 23 is profound. “The steps of a man are established by the LORD, when he delights in his way.” For the believer who delights in God’s way, every step is established. Not random. Not accidental. Even the falls that happen are caught by the LORD’s hand. Verse 24: “though he fall, he shall not be cast headlong.” This is one of the great pastoral truths of the psalm. Christians fall. We sin. We make mistakes. We stumble. But we are not cast headlong, because the LORD upholds our hand. The fall does not become a free fall, because the same LORD who established our steps catches us when we stumble.

Verse 25 is David’s testimony. “I have been young, and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken or his children begging for bread.” This is not a promise of material prosperity, believers do face poverty in this fallen world. But it is a testimony about God’s faithfulness across a lifetime. David has watched. He has paid attention. The righteous get cared for, sometimes in ways that seem miraculous, but always somehow. God does not forsake those who fear him.

The image of the wicked in verses 35-36 is striking. “I have seen a wicked, ruthless man, spreading himself like a green laurel tree. But he passed away, and behold, he was no more; though I sought him, he could not be found.” David is describing what he has watched happen. The villain who seemed unstoppable simply…disappeared. There came a day when his glory was gone, and even the search for his memory turned up nothing. Time is on the side of the righteous.

The psalm closes with a beautiful summary. “The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD; he is their stronghold in the time of trouble. The LORD helps them and delivers them; he delivers them from the wicked and saves them, because they take refuge in him.” This is the architecture of Christian confidence. Not our righteousness, but his salvation. Not our strength, but his stronghold. Not our deliverance, but his hand. We take refuge in him. He does the saving.
connection: Psalm 37 is the wisdom psalm that fits Joseph’s situation, fits David’s situation, and fits the believer’s situation in every age. Yesterday Joseph was thrown into prison for refusing to sin. Today, Psalm 37 reminds us that the righteous are not forsaken. The LORD establishes our steps. We will yet be vindicated.
application: Today, mark the blameless. Verse 37 says, “Mark the blameless and behold the upright, for there is a future for the man of peace.” Take some time today to think about someone you know who has lived a quiet life of faithfulness. Maybe a parent or grandparent. Maybe a pastor or teacher. Maybe a friend who has walked with God through real hardship. Mark them. Tell them what you have seen. And ask God to make you one of those who, in old age, can say: I have been young, and now am old, and I have not seen the righteous forsaken.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to order your steps today, one by one.
Thank him that when you fall he upholds your hand.
Ask him for a long faithfulness that becomes its own testimony.
